questions.question_content: Which HTML tag is used to wrap all the items of an unordered list?
questions.explanation: All items of an unordered list are wrapped inside the <ul> element; each item itself is written with <li>.

questions.question_content: Which attribute is used to specify the image URL in an HTML image element?
questions.explanation: The src attribute of the <img> element holds the URL (source) of the image to display.

questions.question_content: Which group of HTML elements are void elements?
questions.explanation: Void elements have only a start tag and no content or closing tag; <img>, <br> and <hr> are void elements.

questions.question_content: Which CSS property is used to change the bullet style of an unordered list?
questions.explanation: list-style-type changes the marker of list items, for example disc, circle, square or none.

questions.question_content: How are multiple attributes added to an HTML element?

options.content: Only one attribute is allowed, so each extra attribute needs a new element
Inside the start tag, as name="value" pairs separated by commas
Inside the start tag, as name="value" pairs separated by spaces
Inside the end tag, as name="value" pairs separated by spaces

questions.explanation: Attributes are written in the start tag and separated by spaces, e.g. <img src="a.png" alt="Profile">.

questions.question_content: Which effect does adding margin: 15px; to a card container produce?

options.content: It adds 15px of space outside the card's border on all four sides
It adds 15px of space inside the card, between its border and its content
It makes the card's border 15px thick
It adds 15px of space only above the card

questions.explanation: margin creates space outside an element's border on all four sides; space inside the border is created by padding.

questions.question_content:
Write a program that prints the HTML markup of an unordered list (`<ul>`) from the given items.

Print `<ul>` on the first line, then one line per item in the form `<li>ITEM</li>` indented by exactly **two spaces**, and finally `</ul>` on the last line. Remove any leading/trailing spaces from each item.

#### Input
The first line contains an integer `N` (1 <= N <= 50), the number of items.
Each of the next `N` lines contains one item (non-empty text).

#### Output
`N + 2` lines: `<ul>`, then each item as `  <li>ITEM</li>` (two leading spaces), then `</ul>`.

#### Sample Input
```
3
Reading
Cricket
Painting
```

#### Sample Output
```
<ul>
  <li>Reading</li>
  <li>Cricket</li>
  <li>Painting</li>
</ul>
```

test_cases.input:
4
  Watching movies  
Playing chess
CSS & HTML
Travelling

questions.question_content:
Void elements have only a start tag and no closing tag. The HTML void elements are:

`area, base, br, col, embed, hr, img, input, link, meta, source, track, wbr`

Given one line of HTML, count how many times each void element appears.

A start tag begins with `<` immediately followed by its name (letters and digits, starting with a letter), e.g. `<img`, `<BR/>`, `<hr >`. Closing tags (`</p>`) are not start tags. Tag names are case-insensitive: always print them in lowercase.

#### Input
A single line of HTML. Attribute values never contain `<` or `>`.

#### Output
If there are no void elements, print `No void elements`.
Otherwise, print one line `name: count` for each void element found, in the order of its **first appearance** in the line, followed by a last line `Total: T` where `T` is the total number of void elements.

#### Sample Input
```
<p>Hello<br>World</p><hr><img src="a.png"><br/>
```

#### Sample Output
```
br: 2
hr: 1
img: 1
Total: 4
```

An ordered list `<ol>` shows a marker before each item. The marker depends on the CSS `list-style-type` and the list's `start` number.

Print the list exactly as the markers would appear, one item per line, in the form `MARKER. ITEM`.

Marker for position `k` (the first item has `k = start`, the next `start + 1`, and so on):
- `decimal`: `k` as a number (1, 2, 3, ...)
- `upper-alpha`: A, B, ..., Z, then AA, AB, ..., AZ, BA, ... (like spreadsheet column names)
- `lower-alpha`: same as `upper-alpha` but in lowercase
- `upper-roman`: Roman numerals (I, II, III, IV, ..., IX, X, ..., XL, ..., XC, ..., CD, ..., CM, ...)
- `lower-roman`: same as `upper-roman` but in lowercase

Remove leading/trailing spaces from each item.

#### Input
The first line contains the style: one of `decimal`, `upper-alpha`, `lower-alpha`, `upper-roman`, `lower-roman`.
The second line contains the integer `start` (start >= 1).
The third line contains an integer `N` (1 <= N <= 30).
Each of the next `N` lines contains one item. It is guaranteed that `start + N - 1 <= 3999`.

#### Output
`N` lines, each in the form `MARKER. ITEM` (marker, a dot, one space, the item).

#### Sample Input
```
upper-alpha
1
3
HTML
CSS
JavaScript
```

#### Sample Output
```
A. HTML
B. CSS
C. JavaScript
```

test_cases.output:
A. HTML
B. CSS
C. JavaScript
